summary: Elizabeth Guthrie worked in religious and Buddhist studies, earning her PhD from the University of Canterbury by 1994. She served as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago.

Elizabeth J. Harris specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Kelaniya under Ananda W. P. Guruge and Y. Karunadasa, later holding posts at Westminster College and the University of Birmingham.

Elizabeth Mills is an Indologist who completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson between circa 2006 and 2011. She has taught Sanskrit and Pali at the University of Toronto.

Elizabeth Morrison works in Buddhist studies and Sinology, completing her PhD at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She served as an instructor at Amherst College (1998–1999) and held a post at Middlebury College around 2004.
Elizabeth Napper specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and became co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project around 1991.

Elke Rogersdotter, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned her PhD from Umeå University by 2006 under the supervision of Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.

Elliot Sperling worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. After studying at Queens College and completing his PhD at Indiana University, he held posts at Harvard University and served as an associate professor at Indiana University from circa 1987 to 2015.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, where she was an associate professor of religion and Asian studies around 1980.
Emanuela Garatti is a scholar of Tibetology who has held academic posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indology scholar who held positions at Sanskrit Pathashala in Vadtal, Baroda College, and as a Pandit at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library.

Emi Matsushita works in history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under MA supervisor John C. Huntington, she held positions at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State University.

Emil Rödiger was a linguist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1821 to 1825. He held academic posts at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1860) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1860–1874).

Emil Sieg was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Kiel. He held positions at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Kiel, the University of Göttingen, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Emilio Teza worked in linguistics and Indology and studied under Anton Boller. He held academic posts at the University of Bologna, the University of Pisa, and the University of Padua, where he was Professor of Comparative Linguistics and Sanskrit (~1886–1912).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (1993) and the University of California, Berkeley (2003). She held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.
Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht School of the Arts and completed a PhD at Utrecht University (~1963–1970). She later held a post at the University of Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford, and he held a post at the Bangladesh National Museum from circa 1962 to 1991.

Encho Tamura specialized in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. After graduating from Kyushu University and studying at Kyoto University, he held posts at Shitennoji University, Kumamoto University, Kyushu University, Kyushu Historical Museum, and the Fukuoka Prefectural Human Rights Center.

Endo Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1949). He held positions at Nihon Fukushi University, Rissho University, and served as president of Minobusan University (~1992–2000).

Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Mahidol University (~2016–2021) under the doctoral supervision of Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.
